# GENITAL HERPES

## _______________________________________________________________________________

## Immunocompromised patients

## _______________________________________________________________________________

Immunocompromised patients in whom genital herpes simplex disease is often severe include: patients with HIV infection, organ transplants, malnourishment, eczema or severe burns, and in patients receiving immunosuppressive chemotherapy.

## Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat mild to moderate disease for 10 days. In severe disease, treat with intravenous acyclovir for 2 to 7 days based on clinical response, then treat with an oral antiviral for a total duration of 10 days.

## _______________________________________________________________________________

References:
Center for Disease Control and Prevention. MMWR (2021) 70:1-192

Therapy:
## Immunocompetent patients

## _______________________________________________________________________________

Treatment of the initial episode decreases the duration of pain, lesions, and viral shedding by 1 to 2 days. Treatment of the initial episode does not decrease likelihood of recurrent episodes.

Preferred:
Acyclovir 400 mg PO q8h for 7-10 days ($) [R]

Alternative:
Valacyclovir 1 gm PO q12h for 7-10 days ($) [R]

## Episodic therapy for relapses

Treatment of recurrent episodes must be started within 24 hours of symptom onset. Treatment decreases the duration of pain and lesions, and viral shedding by 1 to 2 days. Consider suppressive treatment for patients with more than 6 episodes per year.

Acyclovir 400 mg PO q8h for 5 days ($) [R]
< OR >
Acyclovir 800 mg PO q8h for 2 days ($) [R]
< OR >
Valacyclovir 500 mg PO q12h for 3 days ($) [R]

Alternative:
Valacyclovir 1 gm PO q12h ($) [R]

## Treatment for severe disease

Infectious Diseases consult encouraged.
Acyclovir 5 mg/kg IV q8h ($$) [R]

## Chronic suppressive therapy

Suppressive therapy is indicated in patients with more than 6 episodes per year, or in patients with less frequent episodes who are desiring to minimize risk of transmission. Some patients may find episodic treatment more convenient. The frequency of recurrences can decrease after 1 to 5 years, and suppressive therapy may be stopped every few years to see if it is still needed.

Preferred:
Acyclovir 400 mg PO q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:
\*Note: Recommend increasing dose to 1000 mg per day for patients that have breakthrough on the 500 mg dose. See recommendation below.
Valacyclovir 500 mg PO Q24h ($) [R]

## For patients with 10 or more episodes/year or breakthrough on lower dose:

Valacyclovir 1000 mg PO Q24h ($) [R]
